subject: Neurology
subtopic: Pupillary control and relative afferent pupillary defect
vignette: A medical student shines a penlight into a volunteer's right eye and observes that both pupils constrict. When the light is moved to the left eye, both pupils again constrict. She is asked to identify the structure that carries the efferent limb producing constriction of the pupil contralateral to the illuminated eye.
question: Which of the following structures carries the parasympathetic efferent limb that produces the consensual pupillary constriction?
explanation_correct: Light striking either retina travels via CN II to the pretectal nuclei, which activate the Edinger-Westphal nuclei bilaterally. Parasympathetic fibers run with CN III to the ciliary ganglion, and postganglionic short ciliary nerves reach the sphincter pupillae to produce both direct and consensual constriction. The short ciliary nerves decrease pupillary diameter, accounting for the consensual response in the eye that was not illuminated.

explanation_incorrect.A: Long ciliary nerves are sympathetic fibers from the superior cervical ganglion to the dilator pupillae; they mediate mydriasis, not constriction.
explanation_incorrect.C: The optic tract is part of the afferent sensory pathway beyond the chiasm and carries no parasympathetic output to the iris.
explanation_incorrect.D: The superior cervical ganglion supplies sympathetic fibers for pupil dilation; its interruption causes Horner syndrome rather than pupillary constriction.
explanation_incorrect.E: The infratrochlear nerve is a sensory branch of CN V1 and has no role in the pupillary light reflex.

educationalObjective: The consensual light reflex is mediated by bilateral Edinger-Westphal nuclei with efferent fibers traveling through the ciliary ganglion and short ciliary nerves to the sphincter pupillae.

subject: Neurology
subtopic: Pupillary control and relative afferent pupillary defect
vignette: A 58-year-old patient is given a topical agent that selectively blocks transmission at the ciliary ganglion. The clinician wants to predict which central nucleus normally supplies the preganglionic parasympathetic fibers that would be interrupted.
question: Which nucleus gives rise to the first neuron of the parasympathetic pathway that constricts the pupil?

options.text: Dorsal motor nucleus of the vagus

explanation_correct: The parasympathetic constrictor pathway begins with first-order neurons in the Edinger-Westphal nucleus, which travel via CN III to synapse in the ciliary ganglion. Second-order neurons then travel through the short ciliary nerves to the sphincter pupillae, producing miosis. Blocking the ciliary ganglion interrupts these postganglionic fibers and abolishes pupillary constriction.

explanation_incorrect.A: The pretectal nuclei receive the afferent light signal from CN II and project to the Edinger-Westphal nuclei; they are sensory relay nuclei, not the parasympathetic efferent origin.
explanation_incorrect.B: The superior salivatory nucleus provides parasympathetic fibers to the lacrimal and salivary glands via CN VII, not to the iris.
explanation_incorrect.C: The ciliospinal center of Budge (C8-T2) is sympathetic and initiates pupillary dilation, the opposite of constriction.
explanation_incorrect.E: The dorsal motor nucleus of the vagus supplies parasympathetic output to thoracoabdominal viscera and does not innervate the pupil.

educationalObjective: The first neuron of pupillary constriction arises in the Edinger-Westphal nucleus and reaches the ciliary ganglion via CN III.

subject: Neurology
subtopic: Pupillary control and relative afferent pupillary defect
vignette: A 45-year-old patient has normal pupillary responses. A physiology review asks where the first neuron of the sympathetic pathway responsible for pupillary dilation originates.
question: Which of the following structures gives rise to the first neuron of the sympathetic dilator pathway?
explanation_correct: Mydriasis is sympathetic: the first neuron runs from the hypothalamus down to the ciliospinal center of Budge at C8-T2. The second neuron exits at T1 to the superior cervical ganglion, and the third follows the internal carotid through the cavernous sinus as the long ciliary nerve to the dilator pupillae. Thus the pathway begins in the hypothalamus.

explanation_incorrect.B: The ciliary ganglion is parasympathetic and mediates pupillary constriction through the short ciliary nerves, not dilation.
explanation_incorrect.C: The superior cervical ganglion houses the second sympathetic neuron, not the first.
explanation_incorrect.D: The ciliospinal center of Budge is the destination of the first neuron and the origin of the second sympathetic neuron.
explanation_incorrect.E: The Edinger-Westphal nucleus is the origin of the parasympathetic constrictor pathway.

educationalObjective: Pupillary dilation begins with a hypothalamic first neuron that descends to the ciliospinal center of Budge.

subject: Neurology
subtopic: Pupillary control and relative afferent pupillary defect
vignette: A 30-year-old woman has reduced vision in the right eye from optic neuritis. Shining a light in the left eye causes both pupils to constrict, but when the light is swung to the right eye, both pupils dilate. She is told she has a Marcus Gunn pupil.
question: Which of the following best explains this swinging-light finding?

options.text: A lesion of the right Edinger-Westphal nucleus
A lesion of the left oculomotor nerve
A unilateral lesion of the right afferent limb (retina or CN II)
A lesion of the right superior cervical ganglion
Bilateral destruction of the pretectal nuclei

explanation_correct: A relative afferent pupillary defect results from a unilateral or asymmetric lesion of the afferent limb, such as the retina or optic nerve. When light is shone in the normal eye, both the direct and consensual reflexes are intact; when it is swung to the affected eye, the reduced afferent signal reaches the pretectal nuclei poorly, so both pupils dilate instead of constricting. The efferent pathways themselves remain functional.

explanation_incorrect.A: Damage to an Edinger-Westphal nucleus would impair the efferent constrictor response of one eye regardless of which eye was illuminated, not produce a swinging asymmetry.
explanation_incorrect.B: A left CN III lesion would abolish direct constriction in the left eye but would not cause the characteristic dilation when light is swung from the normal to the affected eye.
explanation_incorrect.D: The superior cervical ganglion is sympathetic; a lesion there would cause Horner syndrome with miosis, not an afferent pupillary defect.
explanation_incorrect.E: Bilateral pretectal destruction would abolish the light reflex in both eyes symmetrically rather than produce an asymmetric swinging response.

educationalObjective: A Marcus Gunn pupil reflects an asymmetric afferent lesion, so swinging light to the affected eye causes both pupils to dilate.

subject: Neurology
subtopic: Pupillary control and relative afferent pupillary defect
vignette: A 60-year-old patient with an internal carotid artery dissection develops right ptosis and miosis. The clinician is tracing the course of the sympathetic fibers destined for the pupillary dilator as they leave the cavernous sinus and enter the orbit.
question: Through which of the following nerves do postganglionic sympathetic fibers reach the pupillary dilator muscle?
explanation_correct: The third sympathetic neuron travels along the internal carotid artery, passes through the cavernous sinus, and enters the orbit as the long ciliary nerve to reach the pupillary dilator. These long ciliary nerves increase pupil diameter, hence mydriasis. A carotid dissection can interrupt these fibers, producing the painful ptosis and miosis of Horner syndrome.

explanation_incorrect.A: Short ciliary nerves carry parasympathetic fibers from the ciliary ganglion to the sphincter pupillae and mediate constriction, not dilation.
explanation_incorrect.B: The oculomotor nerve carries parasympathetic constrictor fibers to the ciliary ganglion and motor fibers to most extraocular muscles, not sympathetic dilator fibers.
explanation_incorrect.C: The trochlear nerve supplies only the superior oblique muscle and carries no sympathetic fibers to the iris.
explanation_incorrect.D: The maxillary division of CN V is sensory to the midface and does not convey sympathetic fibers to the pupillary dilator.

educationalObjective: Third-order sympathetic fibers reach the dilator pupillae via the long ciliary nerve after traveling through the cavernous sinus.
